messages:
pagerduty: [ALERT] Dedicated pool 'aurelia-prod' (dp-73) GPU util 98% >3m. Tenant 'aurelia-corp' accounting for ~92% of GPU memory on all nodes. Potential capacity exhaustion — customer-facing latency/errors. Severity: P1.
opsbot: Incident created: INC-20240315-2412345678. Paging oncall: @sanjay. Runbook: dedicated-pool-gpu-exhaustion.
sanjay: on it, acking pager. grabbing metrics now.
maya: ping — are you the primary oncall? need to decide burst vs degrade.
sanjay: I'm primary. quick summary: all 3 GPUs at ~98% mem, high proportion of mem used by a single tenant workload. looks like very long-context requests (50k token summarizations) from Aurelia.
julian: can autoscaler add nodes? what's max config for this pool?
maya: autoscaler upper bound = 8 nodes, current = 6. cloud quota for pool project is 7 (we hit a quota ceiling last month). autoscaler tried and failed to add 2 nodes earlier. logs show quota deny.
julian: so no automatic burst to 2 more nodes. any policy to burst to shared-hosted? that tenant is on Dedicated TOS that forbids multi-tenant fallback without approval.
sanjay: two mitigation options: 1) manual scale to 7 (allowed) + evict non-critical batch jobs from tenant + rate-limit new requests, and route to smaller quantized model variant for heavy requests; or 2) ask CS+customer to pause bulk runs while we sort infra (slower). prefer 1 for immediate relief.
elaine: I'm on CS — pinging Aurelia on dedicated channel now. asking to pause large backfills for 30m. 
opsbot: runbook step: set tenant throttles and enable fallback model. See commands below.
maya: dropping commands — please run with sudo-redwood role.

```
# set tenant rate limit
redwood tenant update --tenant aurelia-corp --rate-limit 20rps
# set temporary fallback model for heavy requests
redwood route update --tenant aurelia-corp --route /generate --fallback-model xq-7b-quant --reason "emergency memory mitigation"
```

sanjay: applying tenant throttles now.
sanjay: throttle applied -> 20 rps. will escalate if we still see errors.
julian: manual k8s scale command if allowed:
```
kubectl -n dedicated-prod scale sts dp-73-nodetype --replicas=7
```

julian: note: scaling will take ~4-6m to provision and attach GPUs.
opsbot: recommended ephemeral step: evict `batch-worker` pods labeled `job=low-priority` for tenant to free memory.
sanjay: evicting low-priority pods for aurelia-corp now.
```
kubectl -n dedicated-prod delete pod -l tenant=aurelia-corp,job=low-priority --grace-period=30
```

sanjay: eviction command ran, 12 pods terminated. observed ~30% freed GPU mem on node-1 immediately.
sanjay: triggered manual scale to 7 (kubectl sts scale). provisioning in progress.
opsbot: cloud provider quota note: one GPU allocation pending approval for account org-394. created cloud request CR-8942.
elaine: Aurelia responded — they did start a large summarization job; will pause the run for 45m. they asked for a short mitigation plan and ETA.
julian: while we wait for new node, also enable model-level quantization fallback for any request where input_length > 15k tokens to avoid memory spikes.
maya: added policy: if input_tokens > 15000 -> route to xq-7b-quant. implemented via routing rule.
sanjay: new node came up, GPU mem usage dropped to 64% overall. tail latency for Aurelia requests decreased from 2.4s errors -> 220ms median.
opsbot: Incident state: P1 -> P2 (partial mitigation). document: actions_taken = [evicted non-critical pods, throttled tenant, enabled fallback model, manual scale to 7].
elaine: drafting customer note: "We observed an unanticipated burst of very large-context requests. We applied temporary throttles and routing to a quantized model, evicted low-priority background jobs, and manually scaled your dedicated pool to restore capacity. Please avoid heavy backfills until we confirm autoscale/quota updates. We will follow up with RCA and recommended config changes." happy to send after you confirm.
anna: i'll take watch. handing off from @sanjay -> @anna for 2h monitoring. please paste dashboards and checks i should watch.
sanjay: handoff notes: monitor GPU mem utilization (dashboard: /dash/dp-73-gpu), request error rate for tenant (metric: tenant.aurelia.errors), tail lat (p95). if mem > 85% trigger page. also follow up on cloud CR-8942.
anna: ack, taking watch. will escalate if error rate increases.
julian: follow-up actions (owner): 1) infra: request quota bump (owner: julian, due: +24h). 2) product: consider per-tenant backfill protections / large-input soft-limits (owner: maya, due: 72h). 3) ops: add autoscaler fallback to request smaller model variants before scaling (owner: sanjay, due: 48h).
opsbot: log: incident INC-20240315-2412345678 updated with mitigation steps and first-contact message.
sanjay: closing active paging. leaving incident open for RCA and customer comms. thanks all. :thumbsup:
elaine: sending customer note now.
anna: will post a post-incident summary and RCA draft in #postmortems tomorrow morning.
